title: Weak homotopy retractions extend to coherent retraction diagrams
statement: Use the universes, simplicial nerves, quasicategories, coherent functors, homotopies and equivalences of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $R$ be the small ordinary category with objects $X,Y$, morphism sets $\operatorname{Hom}_R(X,X)=\{1_X,e\}$, $\operatorname{Hom}_R(X,Y)=\{r\}$, $\operatorname{Hom}_R(Y,X)=\{s\}$ and $\operatorname{Hom}_R(Y,Y)=\{1_Y\}$, and composition determined by $r\circ s=1_Y$, $s\circ r=e$, $e^2=e$, $r\circ e=r$ and $e\circ s=s$, together with the identity laws. For any quasicategory $\mathcal E$, objects $u,v\in\mathcal E$ and arrows $a:v\to u$, $b:u\to v$ whose composite $b\circ a$ is homotopic to $1_v$, there is a coherent functor $F:N(R)\to\mathcal E$ with $F(X)=u$, $F(Y)=v$, $F(s)=a$ and $F(r)=b$. More precisely, let $\operatorname{Ret}\subseteq N(R)$ be the image of the $2$-simplex with successive edges $s,r$ and long edge $1_Y$; it is $\Delta^2$ with its long edge collapsed to a point. Every simplicial map $\operatorname{Ret}\to\mathcal E$ extends to $N(R)\to\mathcal E$, retaining that whole weak-retraction triangle.

source.place: HTT Definition 4.4.5.2, Remark 4.4.5.5 and Corollary 4.4.5.7, printed pp.304-305 (PDF pp.321-322); the homotopy-category retraction criterion is explained at the start of Section 4.4.5, printed p.303. Ret to Idem+ is inner anodyne by Proposition 4.4.5.6. Read online; no local archive or matching Stacks tag.
